one_liner: In-memory block/frame compressor beating zlib deflate on speed, trading compression ratio for GB/s decode.
what_it_does: LZ4 compresses and decompresses in-memory buffers, giving the caller full buffer control rather than a stream abstraction. The core API (lz4.h) handles single-shot, context-reuse, and streaming block compression; lz4frame.h adds the self-contained, interoperable frame format the CLI and most bindings actually exchange. It is not a drop-in for zlib's API: LZ4_compress_default/LZ4_decompress_safe use different call signatures, and the block format needs the caller to track compressed size and a decompressed-size bound itself.
how_it_is_fast: LZ4 uses a byte-oriented LZ77 variant with a simple hash-chain match finder and no entropy coding stage (no Huffman/range coding like deflate), so both compression and decompression are dominated by cheap memcpy-style literal/match copies instead of bit-level decoding. Decompression in particular is just a sequence of length-prefixed copy operations, which is why it reaches multi-GB/s per core. A tunable "acceleration" factor lets the compressor skip more match-search work for more speed at a lower ratio, and LZ4_FAST_DEC_LOOP enables an optimized decode loop on x86/x64/aarch64.
when_to_use: Hot-path in-memory compression where decompression speed dominates (caches, IPC payloads, columnar/log formats)
Read-heavy data where you decompress far more often than you compress
Need dictionary compression for many small, similar payloads (frame API supports a 64KB dictionary window)
Embedded/freestanding targets: single C90 source pair (lz4.c/lz4.h), optional LZ4_FREESTANDING build removes libc dependency
Already have LZ4_HC available when you need a higher ratio at the same decompression speed but slower compression
when_not_to_use: Compression ratio matters more than speed: zlib -6 (3.099) and zstd both beat LZ4's 2.101 default ratio
Need a drop-in replacement for a zlib/deflate API surface — LZ4's API and block/frame formats are different
Want one universal knob for ratio/speed tradeoffs across a wide range — zstd's level range is broader than LZ4's acceleration + HC split

Pulling in a released package manager build: the current tagged release (v1.10.0, 2024-07-22) predates a 2025-06-01 fix for unhandled NULL-pointer args in lz4frame (CVE-2025-62813); only the dev branch has it
Need built-in multithreading: LZ4 itself is single-thread per call; parallelism is the caller's responsibility

integration.form: source-drop (lz4.c+lz4.h minimum) | static lib | shared lib
integration.dependencies: none for block API; frame API (lz4frame) additionally needs xxhash.c/xxhash.h from the same repo; lz4file adds a <stdio.h> dependency
integration.min_toolchain: C90 (with long long and optional variadic macros); C99+ used opportunistically (e.g. restrict) with a C90 fallback
integration.platforms: any C90 target incl. 32-bit and freestanding/embedded (LZ4_FREESTANDING=1 drops libc); LZ4_FAST_DEC_LOOP auto-enabled on x86, x64, aarch64
integration.thread_safety: not documented in lz4.h beyond context objects (LZ4_stream_t / LZ4_streamDecode_t) being per-call state the caller owns; no explicit thread-safety statement found
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — different API and wire format from zlib, not a compile-time swap

gotchas: Block API (lz4.h) is not self-describing: caller must transmit/store the compressed size and a max decompressed-size bound separately
Advanced/experimental symbols behind LZ4_STATIC_LINKING_ONLY are excluded from the shared-library ABI and can break between versions — static-link only
Repo license is split by directory: lib/ is BSD-2-Clause, programs/ (CLI, tests) is GPL-2.0-or-later; check which files you actually vendor
Open issue #1779 (as of 2026-08) flags the streaming-decompression "synchronized mode" docs as wrong/misleading — verify ring-buffer streaming behavior against source, not just the header comment
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick LZ4 over Zstandard when decompression throughput and minimal-dependency portability (down to freestanding C90) matter more than ratio; zstd's -1 level already beats LZ4's ratio (2.883 vs 2.101) at somewhat lower speed, and zstd exposes a much wider ratio/speed level range, so pick zstd when you want one tunable knob spanning LZ4-like speed to gzip-beating ratio.
verified_claims_summary: First-party lzbench run (LZ4 v1.9.0, GCC 8.2.0, Core i7-9700K @4.9GHz, Ubuntu 4.18.0-17) reports LZ4 default at 780/4970 MB/s (compress/decompress) and ratio 2.101, versus zlib deflate 1.2.11 -1 at 100/415 MB/s and ratio 2.730 — roughly 7.8x faster compression and 12.0x faster decompression at a lower ratio. An independent lzbench 2.0.1 run (gcc 14.2.0, AMD EPYC 9554) corroborates the direction: lz4 1.10.0 at 577/3716 MB/s vs zlib 1.3.1 -1 at 93.0/323 MB/s.
status_note: Actively maintained (dev branch commit 2026-06-01) but the latest tagged release is v1.10.0 from 2024-07-22, so a NULL-pointer-arg fix (CVE-2025-62813, merged 2025-06-01) is not yet in any released tag; usability is 'copyable' since every file carries an OSI license (BSD-2-Clause in lib/, GPL-2.0-or-later elsewhere).
